title: The ordinary consecutive-reduction kernel on a flat-term complex
statement: Let C be a small category and T a Grothendieck topology, A a commutative ring, J an ideal, and n a natural number. Use the constant coefficient reductions and their actual quotient successor [lem-weil-pbc-constant-completion-equivalence, lem-sfb-adic-finite-reduction-data]. Let L be the concrete kernel of A/J^(n+2) -> A/J^(n+1). Multiplication by J kills L, so it has its canonical quotient A/J-module structure; let M be its constant-module sheafification [def-weil-pbc-constant-coefficient-scalar-extension]. For any cochain complex K of constant A-module sheaves with each term flat [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules], the kernel complex of its actual consecutive ordinary reduction map is isomorphic to the termwise tensor of restriction of M with K. No derived category, K-flatness, choice of representative, normalized transition or homology is involved.

source.place: Tag 09C2, proof of (1), successive ideal-quotient coefficient sequence; sites-modules.tex (Modules on Sites), Tags 03CY, 03EK, 03ER, exact module sheafification and flat tensor.

proof.text: Regard the two actual quotient rings as A-modules and their quotient factor as an A-linear map. Its kernel is the concrete RingHom.ker used by the existing residue coefficient module. The inclusion is injective, the factor is surjective by lifting representatives in A, and its zero fibre is precisely the image of the inclusion. ModuleCat.shortComplex_shortExact gives the specified algebraic kernel fork. The already proved annihilation lemma constructs the residue action; the identity on elements identifies its restriction with this algebraic A-module.

Constant module presheaves preserve finite limits because evaluation at each site object is the identity functor on modules. Exact module sheafification therefore takes the algebraic fork to a kernel fork. For a constant scalar map, the sheafification adjunction constructs the restriction comparison; the existing restrictSheafificationComparison_isIso proves it invertible. Applied to the concrete residue module, it identifies the first object with restriction of adicFiniteCoefficientKernelSheaf.

Construct the isomorphism from the constant A-module of each quotient to its restricted regular coefficient sheaf by sheafifying the constant-ring unit. Local injectivity and surjectivity of that unit imply that the comparison is invertible. The sheafification adjunction and naturality of toSheafify show that these comparisons intertwine the specified algebraic quotient factor with the coefficient-ring transition. Compose tensoring these comparisons with the existing natural extensionTensorIso. On pure tensors, pure_map and extensionTensorComponent_pure reduce the consecutive-transition square to the defining pure-tensor formula in reductionStep_existsUnique. This proves the natural tensor presentation for the actual quotient arrows, without flatness or complexes.

Map the sheafified coefficient kernel fork by tensorRight (K.X q); its finite-limit preservation is exactly the first part of hflat q. The inclusions and quotient arrows are natural transformations of tensorLeft functors, so applying mapHomologicalComplex supplies chain maps. Construct the kernel lift componentwise using each limit fork. The chain equation follows by composing with the kernel inclusion and using its universal property, and factorization and uniqueness hold degreewise. Thus the tensor complex is a kernel in complexes. Transport this limiting fork across the normalized reduction isomorphisms, then use uniqueness of kernels and the residue-module restriction comparison to obtain the claimed isomorphism. No additional hypotheses or choices of arbitrary data occur, including for zero or unit ideals.

proof_origin.place: Tag 09C2 finite reduction argument, with the ordinary coefficient kernel supplied explicitly; Tags 03CY, 03EK and 03ER for module sheafification, tensor product and flatness. Complete Lean proof, including the normalized quotient arrow and the universal kernel in complexes.

mathlib_searches.results: Mathlib search returned no matching quotient-tower theorem. Project AdicResidueCoefficientSequence handles the completed-coefficient slice sequence with an additional Noetherian hypothesis and does not specify the quotient arrow; SuccessiveQuotientFlatTensorSequence requires a principal regular element. The sole blueprint quotient tensor match is supported cup product, a different statement. Existing tensor cancellation and extension-tensor comparison are used instead of restating them.

from.place: Proof of Stacks 09C2 (1), the ordinary coefficient-kernel tensor sequence preceding any Tor test or inverse-product argument.

lean.statement:
theorem adicFiniteTransitionKernel_tensor
    {C : Type w} [SmallCategory C] (T : GrothendieckTopology C)
    (A : Type w) [CommRing A] (J : Ideal A)
    (K : Cx (constant T A)) (hflat : ∀ q : ℤ, SheafOfModules.IsFlat (K.X q))
    (n : ℕ) :
    let _ := SheafOfModules.monoidalCategory (constant T A)
    Nonempty ((kernel ((reductionComplex T A J false K).asFunctor.map
        (homOfLE (Nat.le_succ n)).op)) ≅
      ((MonoidalCategory.tensorLeft ((res (quotient T A J 0)).obj
        (adicFiniteCoefficientKernelSheaf T A J n))).mapHomologicalComplex
        (.up ℤ)).obj K)
